summary: 植物在恒定环境中仍显示周期性活动，说明生物体内存在接近一天的节律。文章区分实验证据和流行的“三周期”说法，再追踪大脑、细胞及基因层面的计时研究。
logic: 从微生物考察节律起源

paragraphs.brief: 暗室里的叶片继续开合
sentences: From buffalo to bacteria, oaks to algae, all life follows the same relentless 24-hour cycle, which is driven by the rising and setting of the Sun.
从水牛到细菌，从橡树到藻类，似乎所有生命都随日出日落而遵守同一种周而复始的二十四小时节律。
Or is it?
真的是这样吗？
Over 250 years ago, a French scientist performed a simple experiment that blew apart the idea that all life on Earth does the bidding of the Sun.
二百五十多年前，一位法国科学家用一个简单实验打破了“地球上所有生命都听命于太阳”的看法。
Intrigued by the way some flowers open and close their leaves each day, Jean-Jacques de Mairan put a heliotrope in a darkened room and observed the effect.
让－雅克·德梅兰对一些花卉的叶子每天开合感到好奇，就把一株向阳植物放进暗室观察。
He was expecting the plant, robbed of sunlight, to cease its daily routine.
他原以为，失去阳光后这株植物就会停止每天的活动。
To his astonishment, its leaves continued to open and close as if in response to some invisible timekeeper.
出乎他意料的是，叶片仍然照常开合，仿佛有一座看不见的时钟在指挥。
paragraphs.gist: 德梅兰把一株植物移进暗室后，原以为它会失去作息，叶片却照常开合，显示日常节律能在没有日照时继续运行。

paragraphs.brief: 生物钟与警觉低谷的风险
sentences: But what – and where – is this internal timekeeper?
但这个内部计时器究竟是什么，又在什么地方？
And how does it achieve such astonishing regularity?
它怎样做到如此规律？
These are the mysteries at the forefront of chronobiology, the study of the effect of time in living organisms.
这些都是时间生物学的前沿问题，这门学科研究时间如何影响生物。
The search for answers is about more than just tying up some scientific loose ends.
寻找答案并非只是为了解决几个科学疑问。
Internal ‘clocks’ clearly cause a lot of hardship.
内部的“时钟”显然造成许多困难。
When an individual’s ‘clock’ is knocked out of synchronization through having to work at night or go on long-haul flights, that person can be left utterly unable to think or act.
当一个人的 " 时钟 " 因不得不在夜间工作或乘长途航班而失去同步性时，此人完全无法思考或采取行动。

Yet even when these ‘clocks’ work correctly, the natural rhythms of alertness they generate prove dangerous: traffic accident statistics show two deadly peaks, at 4 a.m. and again twelve hours later when people are at their least alert.
不过，即使生物钟正常工作，它造成的警觉性自然起伏也会带来危险，交通事故统计的两个致命高峰分别是凌晨四点及十二小时后的下午四点，都是人最不警觉的时候。
paragraphs.gist: 研究生物钟既要解释内部计时器的位置与规律，也有现实意义，因为夜班、跨时区飞行以及一天中警觉性低谷都会影响行动安全。

paragraphs.brief: 流行的三周期危险日说
sentences: During the 1970s, best-selling books began to emerge claiming such phenomena were manifestations of so-called biorhythms, a set of three cycles governing physical, emotional and intellectual traits.
二十世纪七十年代，一些畅销书声称，这些现象体现了所谓“生物节律”，即分别支配体能、情绪和智力的三个周期。

Said to start from the moment of birth and repeat every 23, 28 and 33 days respectively, they were supposed to result in ‘critical days’ when one or more cycles led to sub-optimal performance, with unfortunate consequences.
据说三个周期从出生时开始，分别每 23、28 和 33 天循环一次，一个或多个周期状态不佳时就会出现可能带来不良后果的“危险日”。
paragraphs.gist: 二十世纪七十年代畅销书声称，人从出生起便受体力、情绪和智力三种多日周期支配，它们的低谷会形成所谓危险日。

paragraphs.brief: 研究综述驳斥多日周期说
sentences: Scientists have since dismissed biorhythms as pseudoscience, insisting the existence of the three cycles has no basis in fact.
科学家后来把这种三周期说斥为伪科学，指出所谓三个周期的存在缺乏事实依据。
In 1998, Dr Terence Hines of Pace University, New York State published the most comprehensive study of the claims made for biorhythms, reviewing the results of over 130 investigations.
1998 年，纽约州佩斯大学的特伦斯·海因斯博士审查了一百三十多项研究，对三周期说作了当时最全面的检验。
He found that three-quarters of them failed to provide any support for biorhythms.
他发现四分之三的研究完全不支持这种说法。
Most of the remainder contained blunders ranging from faulty mathematics to basic errors in statistics, while the handful of positive studies were explicable as flukes.
剩余研究大多在数学或基本统计方法上有错，少数正面结果也可用偶然巧合解释。
paragraphs.gist: 海因斯审查逾一百三十项研究，大多数未支持这套三周期说，余下不少存在计算或统计错误，少量阳性结果也可用偶然解释。

paragraphs.brief: 无日照时的自由运行节律
sentences: But there is no doubting the existence of 24-hour biological cycles – or, rather, ones roughly 24 hours long.
但毫无疑问地存在24小时的生物循环，或者说大约24小时的生物周期。

Following de Mairan’s pioneering work, other researchers found that when deprived of the cues provided by sunlight, organisms settle down to ‘free-running’ cycles that are close to, but rarely exactly, 24 hours long.
在德梅兰的开拓性工作之后，其他研究人员发现，当失去阳光提供的提示时，生物会沉浸在接近但很少确切到24小时的“自由运行”周期中。
In the case of humans, the cycle is typically around 24.5 hours long.
就人类而言，周期一般为24.5小时左右。
This is the so-called ‘circadian’ cycle (from the Latin meaning ‘about a day’), the length of which is generated by the mysterious internal ‘clock’.
这是所谓的“circadian”循环(拉丁语的意思是“约一天”)，其长度是由神秘的内部“时钟”造成的。
paragraphs.gist: 真正有证据的是近二十四小时的昼夜节律，生物即使脱离日照仍会自由运行，人类在这种条件下的周期通常约二十四个半小时。

paragraphs.brief: 从脑内时钟到细胞时钟
sentences: During the late 1960s, chronobiologists believed they had found the ‘clock’, in the form of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a collection of nerves in a region of the brain known as the hypothalamus.
二十世纪六十年代末，时间生物学家认为已找到生物钟，即下丘脑内一组神经细胞组成的视交叉上核。
Linked to photosensitive cells in the eye, the SCN senses daylight and triggers the release of hormones like melatonin, which keep body functions in synchronization with the time of day.
视交叉上核与眼部感光细胞相连，能感知日光并触发褪黑素等激素的释放，让身体机能与一天中的时间保持协调。
For a few years the SCN was regarded as the ultimate pacemaker – at least in higher organisms such as ourselves.
几年来，SCN被认为是最终的起搏器，至少在像我们这样的较高生物中是如此。
But in 1971, scientists at the California Institute of Technology working with fruit flies found evidence for something truly amazing.
但是在1971年加州理工学院的科学家与果蝇合作发现了一些真正惊人的证据
Fruit flies appeared to have genes affecting the daily rhythm of their behavior – suggesting that there are ‘clocks’ inside each of their cells.
果蝇似乎具有影响日常行为节律的基因，提示每个细胞里都可能存在时钟。
Further evidence for this emerged in 1995, when researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital isolated nerve cells from the SCN, and found they kept up a circadian cycle without help from daylight.
1995 年，马萨诸塞总医院的研究者分离出视交叉上核的神经细胞，发现它们没有日光帮助也能维持昼夜节律，提供了进一步证据。
Finally in 1997, scientists at Northwestern University, Illinois, found a gene that regulates the daily rhythms of cellular activity in mammals.
最后，1997年，伊利诺伊州西北大学的科学家发现了一种基因，控制哺乳动物细胞活动的日常节奏。
paragraphs.gist: 视交叉上核能按光照协调身体节律，而果蝇、离体神经细胞和哺乳动物基因研究进一步显示，细胞自身也有计时机制。

paragraphs.brief: 全身时钟如何保持同步
sentences: The details of how this gene, known as CLOCK, actually works are still being investigated, but they could culminate in better ways of coping with shift-work and jet-lag.
科学家还在研究名为 CLOCK 的基因如何工作，弄清机制可能带来更好的轮班和时差应对办法。
Professor Takahashi, who led the research, says that now that we know that circadian clocks exist throughout our bodies, we will need new strategies and therapeutics to reset all of our cells.
研究负责人高桥教授说，既然现在已经知道昼夜时钟遍布全身，就需要能同时重置所有细胞的新策略和治疗方法。
But how do all the biochemical ‘clocks’ inside their cells stay in synchronization and why did organisms bother to acquire a link with sunlight?
但细胞里的无数生化时钟如何保持同步，生物又为何演化出与阳光相联系的机制？
So far, no-one knows, though there are several theories.
到目前为止，没有人知道，虽然有好几种理论。
For example, sunlight might be useful in keeping the myriad cellular ‘clocks’ in lockstep.
例如，日光可能有助于让无数细胞时钟保持一致。
paragraphs.gist: CLOCK 基因的研究可能帮助处理夜班和时差问题，但遍布全身的细胞时钟如何同步、日照在其中起什么作用仍待解释。

paragraphs.brief: 蓝细菌揭示计时的古老起源
sentences: In the search for answers, researchers are studying the behavior of a microbe called cyanobacterium.
为寻找答案，研究者正在观察一种叫蓝细菌的微生物。
In 2005, a team at Nagoya University, Japan, showed that chemical reactions between three proteins produced by this bacterium ebbed and flowed on a 24-hour cycle.
2005 年，日本名古屋大学的团队发现，这种细菌产生的三种蛋白质之间的化学反应呈二十四小时周期起伏。
Cyanobacterium is the oldest form of life on Earth, so this suggests that cellular ‘clocks’ have existed for over three billion years.
蓝细菌是地球上最古老的生命形式，这提示细胞时钟可能已存在三十多亿年。
All subsequent organisms have followed suit, says Professor Johnson of Vanderbilt University, Tennessee.
田纳西州范德比尔特大学的约翰逊教授说，所有后来的生物都效仿了。
‘Bacteria, fungi, plants and animals all appear to have evolved clock systems independently from each other.’
细菌、真菌、植物和动物似乎都各自独立演化出了计时系统。
Quite why is still unknown.
确切原因还不清楚。
But one thing is clear: the daily routine of life is certainly not a modern invention.
但有一点很清楚，生命的日常节律绝非现代发明。
paragraphs.gist: 蓝细菌仅靠三种蛋白质的反应就能呈现二十四小时节律，提示细胞计时可能已有数十亿年历史，不同生物也可能独立演化出时钟。

items.en: support for an earlier finding from experiments on insects
items.zh: 支持早期昆虫实验结论的证据。
items.why: earlier finding from experiments on insects 对应1971年对 fruit flies 果晶的研究发现。support for 对应后面的 Further evidence for this emerged。这里尤其要注意，题目问的不是“昆虫实验本身",而是“对昆虫实验早期发现的支持"。1995 年的细胞实验进一步证明: 生物钟并不只存在于SCN这个整体结构中，而可能存在于单个细胞内部。同义替换: “Support=further evidence.earlier finding=1971年的发现“insects=fruit flies。

items.en: criticism of the way some research data was analysed
items.zh: 对一些研究数据分析方式的批评
items.why: 题目中的 the way some research data was analysed,指研究者如何用数学和统计方法处理数据。原文批评这些研究中存在: + faulty mathematics: 错误的数学计算。.basic errors in statistics: 基本的统计错误。这正是对“数据分析方式"的批评。blunders 表明作者的评价非常负面。

items.en: reference to a basic test on a plant
items.zh: 提及一项以植物为对象的简单实验。
items.why: 题目中的 a basic test 对应原文的 a simple experiment。ona plant 对应德梅朗将一株 heliotrope 放入黑暗房间。实验的基本逻辑是: 去掉阳光这一外部提示，观察植物是否仍保持原有节律。结果植物依然每天开合叶片，由此暗示生命体内部可能存在独立的计时机制。

items.en: a statement that the length of natural cycles varies slightly between living things
items.zh: 自然周期长度在生物之间稍有差异的说法
items.why: varies slightly 对应 close to, but rarely exactly, 24 hours: 都接近24小时，但并不完全相同。 between living things 对应原文中的一般生物 organisms,以及随后举出的具体例子 humans: 24.5 hours。这说明不同生命体的自由运行周期会有轻微差别。不能选C段的23、28、33天，因为那些属于后来被否定的“生物节律理论",而本题说的是实际存在的自然周期。

items.en: reference to a theory that became popular with the public
items.zh: 提到一种在公众中流行的理论
items.why: 题目中的 a theory 指 biorhythms 生物节律理论。became popular with the public 没有直接写成“受公众欢迎",而是通过 best-selling books 畅销书体现。书能成为畅销书，就说明这一理论曾在普通公众中广泛传播并受到关注。注意D段讲的是科学家后来如何否定该理论。“曾经流行"出现在C段。

items.en: The SCN is able to perceive ________ as a result of connections to the eye.
items.zh: 由于与眼睛相连，视交叉上核能够感知________。
items.why: 题干中的: “Connections to the eye=/inkeda to photosensitive cells in the eye。*。perceive= senses。因此被感知的对象就是 daylight 日光。虽然文章其他地方也出现了 sunlight,但本题定位句直接是 senses daylight,所以最稳妥、最精确的答案是 daylight。

items.en: Several years later, research involving ________ showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain ____ (Q21), or ‘clocks’, in their cells.
items.zh: 数年后，一项以________为对象的研究表明，它们日常活动的时间由细胞中某些________（Q21）调节，这些结构又被称为「时钟」。
items.why: 摘要前面讲的是20世纪60年代未。Several years later 对应后面的 in 1971。题干 research involving…对应原文 scientists…working with…,研究对象是 fruit flies Ri, 必须保留复数形式，答案为两个词: fruit flies。

items.en: Several years later, research involving ____ (Q20) showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain ________, or ‘clocks’, in their cells.
items.zh: 数年后，一项以________（Q20）为对象的研究表明，它们日常活动的时间由细胞中某些________调节，这些结构又被称为「时钟」。
items.why: 题干中的: + the timing of their normal actions=the daily rhythm of their behavior。+ was regulated by=genes affecting. 因此答案是 genes。从语法上看，前面有 certain,后面可以接复数可数名词，原文中也使用了复数 genes。

items.en: Other scientists went on to conduct experiments in the dark that proved that a ________ was maintained by individual SCN cells.
items.zh: 其他科学家随后在黑暗中开展实验，证明单个视交叉上核细胞也能维持一种________。
items.why: 题干中的: + individual SCN cells=从SCN中被 isolated 出来的神经细胞。+ was maintained = kept up。+ experiments in the dark= without help from daylight. 空格前有冠词 a,需要填一个单数可数名词词组，答案为 circadian cycle。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.en: Which TWO of the following problems are stated as being linked with the internal ‘clock’?
items.zh: 下列哪两种现象被认为与体内的“生物钟”有关？
correct: a failure among workers on night-shifts to perform tasks
夜班工人未能完成任务
an increase in casualties on the roads at specific times of day
每天特定时间道路伤亡人数增加

items.en: Which TWO of the following issues relating to internal ‘clocks’ remain to be solved, according to information in the passage?
items.zh: 根据文章，关于体内的“生物钟”，下列哪两个问题仍有待解决？
correct: the reason for living beings forming a connection with the Sun’s rhythms
生物与太阳的节奏联系在一起的原因
the way in which all ‘clocks’ in a single organism are able to stay in step with one another
单一生物体中所有“时钟”能够保持步调一致的方式

pairs: 支持某个发现的进一步证据
the timing of their normal actions
the daily rhythm of their behavior
在没有日光的条件下进行实验
points: 题目中的 a basic test 对应原文的 a simple experiment。ona plant 对应德梅朗将一株 heliotrope 放入黑暗房间。实验的基本逻辑是: 去掉阳光这一外部提示，观察植物是否仍保持原有节律。结果植物依然每天开合叶片，由此暗示生命体内部可能存在独立的计时机制。
题干中的: “Connections to the eye=/inkeda to photosensitive cells in the eye。*。perceive= senses。因此被感知的对象就是 daylight 日光。虽然文章其他地方也出现了 sunlight,但本题定位句直接是 senses daylight,所以最稳妥、最精确的答案是 daylight。
clauses: From buffalo to bacteria, oaks to algae, all life follows the same relentless 24-hour cycle, ….
“which is driven by the rising and setting of the Sun”修饰前面的 cycle。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 cycle，再把修饰信息接回主句。
Most of the remainder contained blunders ranging from faulty mathematics to basic errors in statistics, ….
连接词 while 引出“while the handful of positive studies were explicable as flukes”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Each of our cells has an internal 'clock' which dictates our daily rhythms.
每个细胞都有内部的"时钟" 来决定我们的日常节奏
